intro: と and に both mark the other person in verbs like 会う, 話す and 相談する, but they draw different pictures. と is a two-way arrow: both people take part equally, and either could be the subject ("we met, we talked"). に is a one-way arrow: the action goes from you to the other person, who is its target or receiver ("I told her, I went to see him").

skills.rule: Use と when both sides take part equally ("with"); use に when the action goes one way, from the subject to the other person ("to").
skills.explain:
Ask these questions in order.

1. Is the verb mutual by nature? 結婚する, けんかする, 別れる and anything with 一緒に need two equal partners: と only. 山田さんに結婚する is wrong.

2. Is the verb one-way by nature? 言う, 教える, 聞く (ask), 質問する, 頼む, 電話する, 手紙を書く have a receiver: use に. With と they change meaning: 先生と質問しました means you asked questions together with the teacher.

3. Does the verb allow both (会う, 話す, 相談する, ぶつかる)? Then choose the picture. 友達と話す: a conversation. 母に話す: you tell her something. 妻と相談する: you talk it over together. 先生に相談する: you go to the teacher for advice. 会う: に is the everyday default and the natural choice for running into someone or going to see them, above all a superior (偶然先生に会った); と stresses a meeting both sides arranged. ぶつかる: two moving things collide と; hitting something that stays put (a wall, a pole) is に.
patterns: A と [mutual verb: 結婚する・けんかする・別れる・一緒に…]
A に [one-way verb: 言う・教える・聞く・質問する・頼む・電話する]
A と 話す / 相談する  "with, together"  vs  A に 話す / 相談する  "to, go to for advice"
[person] に 偶然 会う  "run into"

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]、友達[ともだち]{と}長[なが]く話[はな]しました。
examples.en: Yesterday I had a long talk with a friend.

examples.jp: 母[はは]{に}本当[ほんとう]のことを話[はな]しました。
examples.en: I told my mother the truth.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]で偶然[ぐうぜん]先生[せんせい]{に}会[あ]いました。
examples.en: I ran into my teacher at the station by chance.

examples.jp: 来年[らいねん]、姉[あね]は山田[やまだ]さん{と}結婚[けっこん]します。
examples.en: My sister is marrying Mr Yamada next year.

examples.jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しのことを妻[つま]{と}相談[そうだん]しました。
examples.en: I talked the move over with my wife.

examples.jp: 進路[しんろ]のことを先生[せんせい]{に}相談[そうだん]しました。
examples.en: I asked my teacher for advice about my future plans.

contrast.note: Both people are equal participants; you can rephrase it as "A and B did it" (私と田中さんが話した). It also means "together with" for any verb: 友達と映画を見た.
The other person is the target or receiver and need not be active. 田中さんに話した: you spoke, Mr Tanaka listened. 社長に会う: you go to see the boss.
An object that does not move or take part is always に: 車が壁にぶつかった. Two moving things colliding take と: 自転車と車がぶつかった.

mistakes.bad: 姉[あね]は山田[やまだ]さん{に}結婚[けっこん]しました。
mistakes.good: 姉[あね]は山田[やまだ]さん{と}結婚[けっこん]しました。
mistakes.note: Marriage takes two equal partners: 結婚する always takes と, never に (unlike English "married to").

mistakes.bad: 授業[じゅぎょう]の後[あと]で先生[せんせい]{と}質問[しつもん]しました。
mistakes.good: 授業[じゅぎょう]の後[あと]で先生[せんせい]{に}質問[しつもん]しました。
mistakes.note: A question goes to the teacher: に. With と you and the teacher were asking someone else together.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]{に}一緒[いっしょ]に映画[えいが]を見[み]ました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]{と}一緒[いっしょ]に映画[えいが]を見[み]ました。
mistakes.note: 一緒に means both did it together, so the partner takes と.

skills.tip: Could the other person say the same sentence about you, with the same part in it? Then と. If they only receive it, に.
